Bodyguard Inverted Umbrella, Large Windproof Umbrellas for Rain & Sun, Compact Umbrella Reverse Umbrella with Reflective Stripe, Teflon Umbrella for Women Men, Travel Folding Umbrella with Cover Bag Every company seems to think that it can make the "next big thing" in umbrellas. It seems as though I've tried dozens of folding umbrellas that promise "this and that" but ultimately fail in one (or more) of the stated advantages. Most have some type of catastrophic failure after only a few uses, some so bad that they make the umbrella totally inoperable. So it was with some skepticism that I ordered this blue Bodyguard Travel Umbrella. It made a lot of promises on its product page -- but would it work as promised?

Finally I've found an umbrella that delivers on its promises. This Bodyguard Travel Umbrella sells for the impressive price of only $20.99, and puts a very useful collapsible umbrella in your hands. You can tell as soon as you pick it up that it is well-made and durable. It has some heft to it, snaps open with the push of a button, and collapses its canopy when you push the 'close' button. Then all you have to do is push the collapsed canopy down into the handle and your compact umbrella can be put into the supplied travel case.

The extra ribs give it additional strength when using it in the wind. It is probably more likely that it would be blown out of your hand than have the umbrella turn inside out on you. The handle is comfortable, fits my hand well, and has a wrist strap to keep it from the aforementioned potential flyaway. Yup, someone finally brought out a good one.
text_fidelity_b: Bodyguard Inverted Umbrella, Large Windproof Umbrellas for Rain & Sun, Compact Umbrella Reverse Umbrella with Reflective Stripe, Teflon Umbrella for Women Men, Travel Folding Umbrella with Cover Bag

text_fidelity_a:
UP by Jawbone - Large - Mint (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I was looking for people who had similar problems with my UP and saw that several folks had the exact same problem.

First I have owned the original and the 2.0 Up. Mine has been replaced a (if you count the replacement in the works) twice. Mu husband's once. I do not shower with mine or wear it during heavy workouts. It is not very accurate on exercise, so I just log the workout and move on. We bought this because I am a programmer, and my husband is a lawyer so the fact this one reminds you to "get up and move" by buzzing is wonderful. That is about the only thing great about it. BUT it is a _big_ great since if it can save your life I don't care how many of these things I have to go through.

Now for the bad....

I thought mine was the only one that grew bigger. The band starts off fitting loose (i wear the medium), and after a few months it swells becoming tight and uncomfortable. Both bands that have failed have done so at the push button end. It stops working after some kind of firmware failure..or could be battery since it won't hold a charge, or it could be any number of things (the band itself feels mushier than when I first received it) But either way, it worked like a champ until it didn't, then an exchange of phone calls and emails with customer service results in a new band and we start over again.

There is nickel in the silver end cap (I am allergic to it) and if I forget to turn the cap around so the metal does not touch my skin I end up with a wonderful itchy rash. I have painted the ends of my cap with a clear coat of nail polish which lasts about a week before I have to repaint it, but that does fix the nickel problem. Still, with a sizable percentage of the population allergic to nickel (see fit bit recall), you would think they could design a band without it. Make the whole end silicone, or offer two caps in the package, one with the silver, one without.

I exercise regularly but either my activities are not available, or I have to take the band off to swim and it does not record biking accurately so for me the activity tracker is sort of useless. I use other systems to track swimming and biking. I have a very good bike computer and comparing UP data and the bike computer made me laugh.

The sleep tracking algorithm is really strange. It records me in bed and asleep hours before I am asleep, and sometimes does not record that I had to get up and let the dogs out at 3am. and Yes I am hitting the sleep mode making the band go "moon" as we say here. I don't believe the sleep data beyond I hit the moon and wake up and hit the sun... so it tells me the elapsed time between those two button pushes.

Other folks have commented on it, but I cook my own food and a lot of it is asian. So.... food tracker it pointless. I don't eat fast food or things with bar codes I can easily figure out the calories of. Though I do use the tracker to see how much water I have drunk in a day. This is especially helpful on campouts and hikes.

If I get a replacement for this band, I will probably give it to my son and let him wear it. I am ready to find one without nickel and that won't break after only a few months of wear.

Customer service has been terrific. Both my husband's and my replacements have been quick and easy. Though no one believes I know what I am talking about. I am a programmer, my husband is an EE and a lawyer. Please believe me when I say I have done the soft reset and it is not working. I even performed a hard reset... nada, but ok I will do it again with you on the phone...twice, and no it still is not working :-P...OK call me back in two hours when it should be charged... meh.

I have other things to do with my time like make some $$ so I can buy a different band that will work for longer than a few months at a time.

In the end it is a good idea just not executed well.
text_fidelity_b: UP by Jawbone - Large - Mint (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

I believe that using these two hiking poles will improve my posture, give me more sensory input to help me maintain my balance and thus, making it easier to walk further, especially on uneven ground.

The hiking poles come with directions to adjust the poles to the correct length and how to check for stability. There is a chart to give the length of the poles and the poles have the the corresponding numbers printed on them to facilitate adjustment. The grips fit my hands nicely. The poles are light weight and remarkably sturdy.

I am looking forward to trying them out at the beach using the snow tips. My cane and walker are both useless in soft sand. I like that I can get replacement tips if necessary.

I’m attending a wedding out of state next month at a farm/barn type wedding venue. I’m sure these poles will help me maintain my balance on uneven ground better and reduce my fear of falling. I’m probably not ever going to hike the Appalachian trail but these poles will help me to be less fearful of walking on uneven ground.

text_fidelity_a: Klean Kanteen Wide Mouth Single Wall Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Leak Proof Stainless Steel Interior Cap - 40oz - Brushed Stainless I don't know how to rate the sturdiness or durability of such a product.  It's a steel bottle.  If you drop it, particularly when full, you'll put some dents in it.  If you're planning on driving over it with a tank, maybe just get a polycarbonate Nalgene.. And I can't really speak to using this on a campfire, which i know some folks do out in the wild.  What i can say is that I really like this bottle.  It has one flaw:  I'm not a huge fan of the cap.  The cap threads onto external threading and this snugs the lip of the bottle up against a gasket seated in the cap.  If this gasket isn't properly seated, the bottle leaks and more than a couple of times have I thought I closed the cap tightly ( you kind of have to crank it down due to this design) only to realize that, though I had, the gasket was allowing water to slowly leak out.  This is a problem on leather car seats or even in a pack, and though I haven't had any major property loss as a result, i still check this bottle for leaks before i stow it.  Say what you will about Nalgene bottles, but they simply don't have this issue.  Nor does the TKWide line, with an internal threading and o-ring cap, made by this same company..  The gasket itself is removable and i think the tab (which is how you pull the gasket out) might get caught in the lip of the bottle occasionally.  Anyway, I do quite like this bottle and I use it almost everyday now, though I've gotten in to the habit of checking it for leaks every time i use it.
text_fidelity_b: Klean Kanteen Wide Mouth Single Wall Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Leak Proof Stainless Steel Interior Cap - 40oz - Brushed Stainless

text_fidelity_a:
Large 35L Hiking Backpack - Packable Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack Water Resistant Cycling Hicking Small Outdoor Backpack Women Men I admit I am slow to write reviews. I want to see how a product holds up in the long haul.

This HEXIN 35L pack has held up and performed wonderfully!!!

Initially I purchased this to take with me to Ireland because I wanted to do a lot of exploring without dragging around large amounts of bags to encompass my gear. It was still in its comfy EASY TO USE self-pouch when I got to the Emerald Isle.

The first day I really used it was a lovely rainy Irish morning. I put all my gear in, from sensitive electronics to water bottles in the side pouches (hugely helpful to not have to dig in bag for a drink). Stored my inn keys and passport in the inner pocket where they were safe but not easily removed from my pack without notice.

I carried my larger Pixelbook, cameras and assortments; Change of clothes and extra layers to add or shed as needed; snacks and even an extra pair of hike boots in the bottom in case I didn't want to tromp around in wet boots.

There are so many pockets and secure dividers. This pack is well made. I have (before and since) tried a variety of styles and brands and I only swear by Hexin. It has lasted two full years and is still water resistant (and been through a LOT of rain), the zippers are still strong and safely covered. I can be really rough on gear, but I clean it after each adventure and I have had NO issues.

There is also a bright orange whistle which, I have only used for my dog, but is great for a small woman to have in emergency.

I love that I can also stick stuff in the straps in the mesh pockets and under the elastic band. You never know.

The straps and pack are nicely designed so they are always comfortable no matter what I stuff in the bag,

I love that when I am not using it I can fold it down so small that it lays flat in the bottom of my bag.

I am back to purchase another HEXIN now because I have given up on the rest. This is a really great bag. At 35L it holds more than enough gear, clothes, etc., and keeps things protected. I highly recommend it and that does not come lightly.

Bottom line: BEST BAG EVER!!!
text_fidelity_b: Large 35L Hiking Backpack - Packable Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack Water Resistant Cycling Hicking Small Outdoor Backpack Women Men

text_fidelity_a:
Ameriwood Home Jacob Laptop Cart, Cherry Update: Fixed the wobble: I found a board in the shed about the width of the other leg, cut one end at the same angle as the desk, painted it cherry and bam! No more wobble at all.
I read all the negative reviews and though they do have a point, but for my use, this works, and I like it. If it doesn't hold up over time I'll update my review.
Pros:
*price is right
*easy assembly
*looks nice
*Allows me to adjust my chair high enough that my legs are at a 90 degree fold which is much more comfortable than having chair too low at my regular desk.
*Having my screen at eye level and tilted really helps my neck, especially since I can't type without looking at the keyboard.
Cons:
*Yes, a little wobbly
*not easy to adjust height if you will regularly want to do so.

To address some of the wobble concerns, the individual components are sturdy, where the desk part slips into the base is where the wobble comes from. I took a plastic "wobble wedge" (available on Amazon) and secured it in the gap, not a perfect fix, but improved the situation. Use real tools to tighten all the bolts and screws, not the tools included in package.
I also used a common plastic door jam to wedge under the uneven wheel.
I do data entry on a calendar, I type for 30 seconds at a time in between calls. When my hands are on the computer, I try to keep the heels of my hands steady, too much hand motion will create a slight wobble. If you are using this for a business where you type long emails or are a student writing papers, you might want to invest in something sturdier. I've seen ones in stores for $130 that are no better than this one.
text_fidelity_b: Ameriwood Home Jacob Laptop Cart, Cherry

text_fidelity_a:
Klean Kanteen Single Wall Stainless Steel Food Canister Container with Leak Proof Stainless Steel Interior Lid I love this canister! It is heavy, sturdy and incredibly durable. This is my fourth purchase from the Klean Kanteen company and I've been incredibly pleased with everything I have purchased. This canister is no exception!

I got tired of knocking over the orange box of baking soda in my pantry and began looking for a stainless storage jar. Most of the stainless pantry jars had poor reviews and were so thin you could deform them with your bare hands. I wanted something that could withstand lots of bangs and bumps if I decided to throw the baking soda in the chuck box for a camp out. (Baking soda + water makes a great first aid paste for bites and stings.) When I stumbled across this one, I knew it would be ideal.

The 16 ounce canister easily held the full 16 ounce (1 pound) box of baking soda with room leftover to stash a small scoop. At 3.75 inches tall and 3.5 inches wide, it doesn't take up a ton of room on my pantry shelf but I no longer have to deal with gritty white baking soda spilling all over the tile floor of my pantry and lingering in the grout lines until I vacuum every nook and cranny. I also like that it will protect my baking soda from absorbing any stray odors that may affect the flavor of my cookies and baked goods.

I took a chance and ordered this one Used - Like New from Amazon warehouse deals. They said it had surface imperfections affecting less than 10% of the surface area. When mine arrived it had a sticker stuck on the lid and residue from another sticker on the side of the canister. It took around 10 drops of Goo Gone and doTerra wild orange to get all the residue off. I thought that was the only "surface imperfection" but then I noticed there are faint scratches along the circular rim of the lid, as if the lid was twisted against a slightly rough surface. Buffing with a drop of orange essential oil helped reduce the appearance of the scratches. Buying used saved me about $3 but be aware that if they say it is scratched, it really is scratched and may or may not have stickers all over it. Buy new if you don't keep Goo Gone on-hand...

In short, I am very, very pleased with this canister and am now wanting to purchase the 8 ounce size to store baking powder in. If you are considering stainless steel pantry storage containers, I highly recommend the thickness, heft and durability of this brand!

Vinyl Label: Oracal 631 color: Mint 055 • Font: KG Call Me Maybe • Craft Cutter: Silhouette

Update: I ordered the smaller 8 ounce container for storing baking powder and I LOVE it! Baking powder is sold in 8 oz containers and this canister easily held one whole can. This pair looks so handsome on my pantry shelf! I am happy that I invested in Klean Kanteen’s high quality stainless storage containers that are going to last my family for years.

Update October 2016: I have just ordered my third Klean Kanteen canister to store pink Himalayan sea salt. The trio continues to look very handsome on my baking shelf! After six months of use I am still very pleased with the investment I have made. The stainless steel is still clean and not dented anywhere because it is sturdy and thick. I'm also noticing improved volume when I bake because the baking powder is kept airtight, away from Houston's horrible humidity so muffins pop out of the oven big and fluffy. I wish I had thought to buy these years ago!
text_fidelity_b: Klean Kanteen Single Wall Stainless Steel Food Canister Container with Leak Proof Stainless Steel Interior Lid

Pactrade Marine 13 1/2" Destroyer SS 304 Steering Wheel 5 Spoke Teak Wood Cap This is a very nice, solid, sturdy Destroyer wheel. I have a 16 ft. center console and when I replaced the steering gear (steering box, cable) I wanted to put a new wheel on the boat too. The old wheel (heavy emphasis on the word "old") was made of some sort of plasticized hard rubber and it was frankly nasty. Years and years of hand oil, motor oil, motor fuel, fish slime and general grunge had accumulated on and eaten up the wheel. It was time to find a new wheel.

It's hard finding the right size Destroyer wheel because I needed a 13 inch wheel and most of them are bigger. A 13 inch wheel is all that will comfortably clear everything else on the console. Many of the wheels I looked at cost around twice as much as this one did.

The wheels spokes are gathered and locked into a central star and a cover made of what looks like teak wood snaps over the top. The description says "bakelite cover" but mine doesn't look like bakelite, nor does the product picture. Mine looks like the one in the picture. My boat, being a center console, has grab rails around the console but I often find myself using the wheel as a grab hold when moving around on the boat. I'm not a small person, so that's likely considerable stress on the wheel itself. It's not a problem, I've been using this wheel for several months and it's as solid as the day I mounted it.

This wheel is rock solid and a perfect finishing touch for my new steering system. I'm very happy with it and never have hand/fish/oil/fuel/grunge on my helm any more!
text_fidelity_b: Pactrade Marine 13 1/2" Destroyer SS 304 Steering Wheel 5 Spoke Teak Wood Cap

I do love it for the HR monitor, and sleep tracking is a lot easier on the HR (having to put on that wristband to track via the One was an added annoyance). And the caller ID feature is cool.

But there are two things I don't like as well. First, I have a very petite wrist (small bone/frame). The Charge HR looks huge on my wrist, and really doesn't sit well. The inflexible part with the face sticks out beyond my wrist, where on someone with a bigger wrist it would flex where it needs to bend around. Hard to explain!

The other thing, which is probably related, is that when I wear a winter coat, the sleeve pushes the FB down on my wrist where it digs in and hurts.

This isn't significant unless you are competing against others rather than just against yourself like I do, but I think the Charge HR counts more steps than my One does. I haven't changed my routine, but I find I'm hitting my 10,000 much earlier in the day than before.

Oh, and I have to charge the HR more frequently than I did the One.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) I wanted this specifically for its heart rate monitor and sleep monitor--something I can basically wear all the time. I specifically did not want a watch, because I wear a watch on my other arm. So this is just right for that. It's a tad bigger than it ideally could be. I hope future generations will slim down and maybe be more flexible and/or add more interesting sensors.

The sleep monitor seems to work okay. I previously had a Microsoft Band 2, and I feel it may have been better at that.

Since I don't use it as a watch, I like the option to turn off the feature to show time when lifting it up. So it stays black unless I really want it to show me something.

It lets you set like 7 alarms, which can repeat, and I use them to remind myself to drink water. So that's a nice plus.

It does seem a little slow to sync. Specifically, I often want to set a silent alarm right before bed, and it takes like a minute to sync. Then I set the alarm, and it takes several seconds to sync that. Then I can finally turn it on, and wait a few seconds to sync that. Pretty cumbersome. The Microsoft Band let you set it quickly on the Band, so it's much better in that way. (But my Band broke during normal use, and I went through a LOT of trouble to get Microsoft to replace it. A lot. Very bad customer service, so I can't recommend it.)

The battery life is good on this, but it's not great. That said, it's much easier to charge than the Blaze, which I also tried. I basically just charge it while I'm in the shower (a trick I learned for the Band), and that's more than enough. I have to say, I have almost gotten in the shower with it a few times. It is easy to forget you have it on!

So I think it's probably the best continuous HR and sleep monitor option that is specifically not trying to pretend to double as a smart watch.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

text_fidelity_a: Ringside Quick Wrap Gel Shock MMA Boxing Hand Wraps My husband and I have a heavy bag we use for punching drills in our house. For years we have used the wraps that we put on under gloves. When our wraps degraded after much use, we had already decided to give gel quick wraps a try when it popped up as something to try for free in exchange for reviewing the product. We got the L/XL size. I have short fingers, but a wide palm and measured riiight on the edge of medium-Large. My concern was if it would fit my small wrists. Much to my surprise everything fit because the wrist can be cinched tight with the Velcro strap. Fingers fit, not too tight with correct separation between knuckles. A few test punches of the bag with just the gel wrap and I was ready. The real test was wearing them in our ringside gloves. It has a very different feel than the long wraps, but the gel cushion was where I noticed a difference. I haven’t used them for very long, but I have arthritis in my knuckles and I didn’t feel pain after I was done. My husband tried them on too. They fit his wrist better, but the rest fit the same. I’m not sure if the gel will last a long while as most equipment with gel in them does degrade, but it it lets me punch the bag without pain, I will keep buying. It is everything you expect and I feel like the manufacturer has gone above and beyond when it comes to the hardware on this jump rope.

First, the handles are my favorite. They have an internal metal ball that swivels effortlessly through a sturdy plastic collar. This set up creates the most effortless jump rope turning you have ever encountered. All you need to do is flip the rope in the direction you want it to go and the ball bearings seem to do the rest with the smallest flicks of your wrists.

The cable is exactly that - sturdy wire CABLE - with a protective plastic coating. It whips through the air and it doesn't hurt that much at all if it strikes you when you misstep (and that is coming from someone who bruises easily). The cable can kink if you fold it and pinch it really hard, which is probably why the seller includes a second cable so you don't have to order a whole new jump rope nor jump with a wonky, crinkled cable. The hardware that makes the jump rope adjustable is really neat and unlike anything else I have seen. It's actually a tiny screw-bolt on each end of the rope that tightens down onto the cable giving you a no slip sizing option. Again, this is a very thoughtful touch, both for those who are tall and short. (The jump rope worked just fine for my 5'10" hubby and 5'7" me.)

The green color is not quite the electric neon color shown but is more a pleasant grass green. I uploaded a picture taken in natural light so you can get a good idea of what the color is like in real life. It's a great unisex color that is not too girlie and is easy to spot in your gym bag or the stash of work out at home gear. It was easy to roll up after using and slides effortlessly back into it's nylon storage pouch.

I was fortunate to be able to purchase this product at a discount to try it out and write a review. This jump rope is not junk, this is a quality fitness item that has had some impressive thought and effort put into its design. Rest assured you are buying a good, quality item!

Bryton Rider 420T GPS Cycling Bike Computer (Cadence+HRM sensors Bundle), 35hrs Long Battery Life, Bread-Crumb Trail with Turn-by Turn Follow Track. 5 Satellites Systems Support for Extreme Accuracy. This is such an incredible cycle computer for this price. I primarily use it to track the basics: speed, cadence, distance. And sometimes I use the map feature. Functionally it has everything I need.

The button interface can be a bit confusing and frustrating to novices. Almost counterintuitive. However, after a few rides it becomes a non-issue. Its a clunky UI and I bet that this may be the swan song of non-touch UI on devices with this level of functionality.

I found the route/map features laggy and frustrating to use on device and app, so I navigate with my phone since it is much, much easier. I CAN use the maps, its just that the UI and responsiveness add 'friction' to the map interaction making it less pleasant than it should be. If you want to leave your phone at home you definitely can, you just have to work at it.

Screen size and configurability of info display is perfect. Phone app is surprisingly good as well. Not the best UI, but much better than I expected and once you fiddle with it for 30 minutes you will grok it.

Holds a decent charge for daily commuting and weekend riding usage. I recharge once a week to be safe, but could probably go longer.

I'm using it on my Dahon Vigor D9 folding bike with a Tern Andros stem. The 420 fits nicely in the center of the Andros (see pic).

If you're thinking about getting this - do it. You won't be disappointed.
text_fidelity_b: Bryton Rider 420T GPS Cycling Bike Computer (Cadence+HRM sensors Bundle), 35hrs Long Battery Life, Bread-Crumb Trail with Turn-by Turn Follow Track. 5 Satellites Systems Support for Extreme Accuracy.

text_fidelity_a:
Splatterburst Targets - 12 x18 inch - Silhouette Splatter Target - Easily See Your Shots Burst Bright Fluorescent Yellow Upon Impact - Made in USA It's really nice to see what you're looking at without having someone else point out the results or to have to use a spotting scope. While I use the smaller Splatterburst Targets to sight in new .22 rifles and pistols, I prefer the larger ones for heavier calibers. Yeah, they work well for long-range target shooting, but for me they are priceless for 7-15 yard practice with my concealed carry weapons. I use a similar drill when sighting in my new .22's, taking the initial shots at the large center mass target and then fine tuning my shots using different ammo manufacturers/configurations to find out which ammo performs best in which gun.

I used to think that a North American Arms .22 magnum revolver would be all that I'd need to defend myself, but slowly I've come around to having enough stopping power to either intimidate someone or put them down with one shot. At a minimum I'll carry a 9mm but I prefer a subcompact .45acp. The trick is to properly conceal a larger weapon so that it doesn't "print" so that someone notices it AND have the ability to easily pull it from concealment and put into service. Whatever weapon you choose, you need to practice being smooth and consistent to develop the efficiency and confidence to bring it into play effectively.

These Splatterburst targets allow you to immediately see what your results are each time you engage it. While shooting paper is not the same as defending yourself in a highly stressful situation, knowing your weapon and what you are capable of doing with it comes with a lot of practice.

NOTE: My apologies to those who might not think that concealed weapon carry is important. On the other hand, "when seconds count, the police are only minutes away".
text_fidelity_b: Splatterburst Targets - 12 x18 inch - Silhouette Splatter Target - Easily See Your Shots Burst Bright Fluorescent Yellow Upon Impact - Made in USA

Intex Mariner Inflatable Boat Set Series I live in an apartment in Arizona, and I wanted a quality inflatable boat I could take to the local lakes. After researching my options, IM4 appeared to be the top boat.

Although manufacturer claims it is a 4 person boat, it is NOT true. Two people can be comfortable in this boat, three is pushing it. With the semi-solid floor the boat is stable on the lakes; however, you cannot stand or dance as some reviewers claim. Solid floor allows it some degree of stability, but not enough to stand up or walk while being fully upright.

The hull materials and ores supplied are very good. Boat has a solid feel to it. When inflating it to the max, it become very firm- raft like.

For $220 this is an amazing deal. I would recommend this boat!

Update from 10/05/2012. On my recent trip to the lake I broke one of the ores. The plastic on the coupling broke when I did five spirited rows, I was upset. I had to try to canoe paddle the boat to shore and mend the plastic coupling with some duct tape! Upon returning home I checked the Intex's website for the replacement coupling; it is being sold for $4+ shipping. Can't blame the boat for the broken ore, plastic coupling is the cheapest part of this boat.
text_fidelity_b: Intex Mariner Inflatable Boat Set Series

WataChamp Bobbin Winder (Gray) Let's start with the product quality. It appears to be very good. Well made, heavy materials, the resistance knob works well as does the line gasket. I'd say it's a good value for the price.

Next, let's talk about how it preforms. Okay, I didn't like it. Not because of the product, but due to my lack of skill. I'm attempting to make PR knots and had a real issue getting the tension right. Curls in the line because I had the tension too tight. Then knots that didn't hold because I had it too loose. I also got things tangled trying to spin it around the line and to be honest made a big mess of things. After several attempts I decided to give up.

If you want to experiment with various fishing knots this may be a good, inexpensive, way to try your hand at the techniques. However, plan on spending a lot of time and line perfecting things. It's a skill that takes plenty of time to master.

I'm not a saltwater fisherman. The heaviest line I use is #30 braid. Usually to #8-#12 leader material. I don't need a knot that holds hundreds of pounds. I'm sure if you do this is a good investment of time and money. I'll just stick with my improved Albright knot.

One last comment. I do use a wrap knot for 7 stand wire leaders on occasion. Forceps work well for that in the past, but I'm guessing this will make some really tight and clean wraps. Haven't tried it yet, but that could be the ticket.
text_fidelity_b: WataChamp Bobbin Winder (Gray)

Cobra 2017 Golf Men's King F7 Driver Connect No amount of technology will ever completely straighten out my slice. Only practice will do that. However, with that being said, and coming purely from an at best, occasional golfer, I've been able to hit balls further than ever with this driver. By adjusting where the weight goes, I've been able to cut down on the severity of my slice and have hit balls straighter on a more frequent basis. I enjoy the driver and the adjustable loft is an added bonus. I set it at what I think will work and leave it at that. Again, my inexperience doesn't allow for a consistent golf swing so I'll sometimes launch it into the stratosphere or run it a foot off the ground for seventy five yards--or something in between--regardless of the loft setting. In addition, the handle was so high when depressed that the chuck couldn't be inserted into the clamp on the bottom outside.  The biggest problem was the poor performance of the chuck on my tubeless tires.  As I tightened the chuck it rotated the valve around the retaining nut, often loosening the nut and the valve body until air leaked out of the tire. YOUR Pillow! by SHO - Ultimate Self Inflating Travel, Camping & Festival Pillow • Total weight with stuff sack, including the plastic slider on the end to keep the sack closed, is 316 grams or 11.25 ounces according to the electronic scale we use to weigh backpacking gear.

• 18 inch circumference and 6 inches long when sat on to squish as much air out as possible and re-rolled tightly after being inflated for use.

Great lightweight camping pillow! My husband went to Philmont this past July and wished he'd had this with him. He takes ultralight backpacking to the extreme and said that the dirty clothes he used as a pillow for 2 weeks were not comfortable at all and in the end were not a wise decision. A few ounces would have been worth the additional comfort. After trying out this most recent purchase, he said he wished he would have had this pillow. It met his requirements for light weight, although the pillow repacked in it's own brown nylon stuff sack is 18 inches in circumference and about 6 inches long, which is larger than what he prefers to carry. (Like I said, he's a tad overboard on the ultralight backpacking...)

The example image colors are way off, by the way. There are NO pink or purple diamond shapes. The colors are solid aqua blue, lime green and dark green stripes together to make an apple green shade, aqua blue and gray stripes together (what looks like purple in the example image), solid red orange, red orange and yellow stripes together, solid yellow, red orange and fruit punch red stripes (appears hot pink in example image) and red orange and yellow stripes, which look tangerine orange in the example image but are darker orange in real life. At first I thought my husband had been fortunate to receive a pillow with no pink or purple diamonds in that part of the pattern but then I realized the example image was just wonky. It is a multi-colored pillow but it's not nearly that bright or little kid-ish looking. It's honestly unisex colored and fine for an adult, teen or child.

The pillow has some soft fluffy fill fibers in it that add to the cushioning but they also suck down quite flat for storage. He liked that aspect, too.

If my picky, "every gram counts" so he went without a pillow for 2 weeks hubby approves of this then it will probably work great for your backpacking excursions, too!
text_fidelity_b: YOUR Pillow! by SHO - Ultimate Self Inflating Travel, Camping & Festival Pillow

Electric Foot Warmer for Men and Women with Non-Slip，Fast Heating Pad with Four Layer Temperature Locking System,Foot Warmer Under Desk.Electric Foot Heating pad with 3 Temperature Settings. The foot warmer seems to be made of good quality fabric and leather.

The foot warmer has three temperature settings: 38C (100F), 42C (108F), and 55C (131F). When I turned the foot warmer on at room temperature, it listed 22C. I adjusted the temperature to the hottest setting of 55C. I kept it going for 45 minutes, with both my feet in the warmer. After 20 minutes or so the warmer stabilized at a temperature of 43 to 44C. 25 minutes later, the temperature had not changed, never reaching anywhere close to 55C. 44C was warm enough, but not what was promised.

Besides the temperature limit, two drawbacks for me (may not apply to other people):
- The foot warmer has USB-C input, and it comes with a USB-A to USB-C cable. Note that the warmer only accepts 10W, and if you try to use a USB-C to USB-C cable that delivers higher wattage, the foot warmer will not work. Ideally the foot warmer's electronics would be designed to take as much wattage as they need, and no more, in the same way I can connect an iphone and an ipad pro to the same fast-charging brick, and each device would accept only as much wattage as appropriate, instead of burning out or shutting down.
- This foot warmer seems to be designed for those who shoe sizes 11 and under. I wear size 13 shoes, and my feet barely fit, with my toes partially curled. Pretty uncomfortable. The product description makes no reference to foot size, and unfortunately for me, I cannot use this foot warmer effectively. Otherwise, it does its job well.
text_fidelity_b: Electric Foot Warmer for Men and Women with Non-Slip，Fast Heating Pad with Four Layer Temperature Locking System,Foot Warmer Under Desk.Electric Foot Heating pad with 3 Temperature Settings.

Kryptonite New York Cinch Ring Security Chain (12mm x 75cm) withEVS4 Disc 14mm Shackle My experience with Kryptonite goes back to the period when one of their their original locks was found to be easily opened with a ballpoint pen. I had registered two of their motorcycle disc locks at that time and as soon as they changed the design they sent me two new replacement locks. Since then I have become older and moved from motorcycles to bicycles.

I previously submitted a review of the very excellent Saris Bike Porter 2-Bike Trunk Rack, which has design features that enable bikes to be securely locked to the rack and also allow the rack to be locked to the frame of my car, under the rear bumper. Kryptonite's 2.25' New York Noose is just the right length to lock the top tubes of two bikes to the beefy upper section of the Saris rack with their Evolution Series 4 Disc Lock, and their KryptoFlex 3/8" x 7' Double Loop Security Cable is perfect to go through the front wheels of both bikes and lock the bottom frame of the rack to the frame of my car with one of the replacement locks they sent me many years ago, which is similar to their current KryptoLok Series 2 Disc Lock. Both of these Kryptonite locks, and the chain and cable, work perfectly and I have never encountered any problems with them.

We don't need this level of security for most of our bicycle outings, but when we head out for a vacation with our bikes that includes stays at multiple motels we always use our Kryptonite locks and chains.

One final note - Although I am sure no one else at Amazon would make this foolish mistake, when we left our B&B to head home from our last vacation I locked up the bikes and then left my cord with the keys to both locks draped over one of the handle bars while I checked the pressure on our car tires for the trip home. Of course I forgot about the keys and did not notice they were missing until we got home and tried to take our bikes off the rack. Luckily I was able to go into our house and get the spare keys that came with the locks. When I ordered replacements from Kryptonite they sent me new keys for both locks at no charge. Kryptonite provides excellent locks and they also provide excellent customer service!

I was looking for a foldable bike to put in a car trunk. Other similar bikes, just half the price, are all shipped from china with 2-3 month wait time with no reviews or 2-3 reviews with 5 stars. Granted they all are made in the same shop from the same chinesium but this one has 30+ positive and was delivered in 4 days.
The good. Frame is steal and well welded and painted. Its heavy but sturdy. Front fork is just as good but has a little play in the springs, not critical. Rear suspension is good enough. Rims are straight.
The so-so. I am 5-11 and set the seat is almost as high as it gets. The handle bar could be higher at my preference.
The bad. Worst thing - the brake disks mounting. Front wheel all six and four on the rear wheel had broken threads. This is a major screwup as the wheels are all aluminum and the only way to fix it is to thread next size 6mm threads. Techicaly, easy fix but this should never happen! Next - the shifters are the cheapest i have seen. The left 3-grear broke while adjusting it. The push lever was grinding the base that caused the latch pin to deflect. I expected to replace them anyhow so it wasnt a show stopper.
And the special thing - the hand pump. This bike comes with a hand pump. I dont know what happened to it, either a $1-per hour laborer or rats on the container ship, either one is a shame for a bike with this price tag, but the pump was all chewed up. Dont believe me - see the pictures
So, two things, the disk brake screws and shifter - two stars,
I would not recommend this bike but there are not too many alternatives. Well, unless you are willing to take the risk and order one from china with no reviews.

text_fidelity_a:
Condor Tool & Knife, TRT (Tactical Rescue Tomahawk), Paracord Wrapped Handle with Sheath I own several Condor sharp-edged tools and have never been disappointed in any of them. My collection of Hatchet/Tomahawk/Breaching Tools includes cheap models from United Cutlery to expensive tools from RMJ Tactical and the Busse family. You can break the cheaper ones with little effort so it's important to distinguish between "pretty or tacticool" and durable/useful. If you want an all-purpose tactical rescue tool this $50.00 Condor TRT is probably the cheapest one that I would trust to perform consistently in a tough environment.

It came out of the box razor sharp -- as in sharp enough to slice a piece of paper. There is a nice sheath that fits over the head but you'll need to stretch it and work it to snap the first time. The sheath also has a belt loop on it for side carry. Now why would I give it four stars instead of five? First off the paracord wrapped handle is slippery. You can remedy that with some sandpaper and create a grip that you are comfortable with.

But the biggest problem is in the weight distribution. This is a full tang hawk with a hollow steel handle and the head is offset to one side. Strange construction that but probably an attempt at keeping this TRT hawk from being too heavy. The strength and durability of this tool is not a concern but the strange (lack of) balance is. Shifting more weight to the head would balance it more properly and make the damage inflicted by the downward strike all the more devastating.

All-in-all though this $50.00 Condor TRT is probably worth twice as much as it costs. Just be aware that it has some drawbacks that might affect your performance with it. If things get too bad you can simply turn it upside down and grip it just below the blade to deliver a heavy handled blow.
text_fidelity_b: Condor Tool & Knife, TRT (Tactical Rescue Tomahawk), Paracord Wrapped Handle with Sheath

SainSmart Jr. Kids Bow and Arrows 2 Sets, Light Up Archery Set with 6 Suction Cups Arrows, Outdoor Hunting Game for 8-12 Toddlers I bought this bow and arrow set for my 3-year-old granddaughter. It is recommended for ages 4-8, so she’s a little young, and indeed it took her a bit of practice to master loading, drawing, and releasing an arrow. It’s been great training for both fine and gross motor skills.

The bow doesn’t have flexible limbs to power the arrows, like a traditional bow. Instead, it has rigid limbs and an elastic string that really does send the suction cup arrows sailing. Our favorite thing is shooting it at the sliding glass patio door. When the arrows fly true, they stick to the glass with a satisfying “splat”. We also like to shoot the stuffed chairs and sofa in the living room. We’ll shoot our bows outside once it warms up and some of the snow melts.

The bow has built-in LED lights that come on and start flashing when you grip the handle. That was an immediate hit with our toddler, and drew her to the bow right away. We mostly ignore that now. I don’t know how long the batteries will last but I expect that by the time they die, she will be more interested in sending arrows across the room than watching the flashing lights. Who knows - maybe this will be the start of a longer term interest in real archery.

Let me know if you found anything in my review helpful.
text_fidelity_b: SainSmart Jr. Kids Bow and Arrows 2 Sets, Light Up Archery Set with 6 Suction Cups Arrows, Outdoor Hunting Game for 8-12 Toddlers

text_fidelity_a:
Fitness Reality Squat Rack Power Cage with | Optional LAT Pulldown & Leg Holdown Attachment | Squat and Bench Rack Combos| Super Max 810 XLT | I'm extremely pleased with the product. Assembly was straightforward and all the holes lined up! Very sturdy construction.

The attached pictures show an addition I made to turn give the rack a cable-crossover functionality. These pictures represent my Version 1.0.

All the parts can be purchased at Lowes. The rack has two perfect attachment points for the pulleys. See picture 1. This shows a threaded eye bolt and 1 1/2" fixed pulley. Two lock nuts hold it in place but it is purposely NOT tight so it has the ability to rotate. Picture 2 shows a length of zinc coated square steel tubing from Lowes. Three threaded eye bolts connect the additional cables to the center cable on the rack. Picture 3 shows me pulling on the two handles.

I think this works really well. Keep in mind, this is Version 1. One could probably cut the steel tubing length down. With the full length, it doesn't seem to hit the cage but it potentially could. NOTE: I did try this without the steel tubing and I didn't like the feel. As one completes the motion, the angle change in the cables was significant enough to notice. Your mileage may vary and you may prefer that characteristic. That tubing was the most expensive piece at about $20. Everything else is dirt cheap.

If you decide to try something like this, please be EXTREMELY careful. I am a Mechanical Engineer by education so this was something I was comfortable doing. Review the load limits of ALL the components you intend to use. For instance, the two fixed pulleys from Lowes have a safe working load of 420 pounds. I used 1/8" vinyl coated braided wire rope. Blue Hawk brand with a safe working load of 340 pounds.

Make sure ANY carabiners you use to make connections are rated for HIGH LOAD and NOT for hanging keys on your belt loop. I can't stress this enough. You do NOT want something breaking on you during full extension.

IMPORTANT: Make sure you terminate the ends of the cables correctly. Properly swaged deformable collars are likely the best approach but I used a threaded clamp for this setup. I will likely change to a swaged connection because the clamping hardware can rub against your arm during use. Also, use thimbles on the ends of both cables to protect the cable attachment points.
text_fidelity_b: Fitness Reality Squat Rack Power Cage with | Optional LAT Pulldown & Leg Holdown Attachment | Squat and Bench Rack Combos| Super Max 810 XLT |

I had been especially interested in the sleep monitoring function, but find it pretty useless. First, the arm band needed to hold the Fitbit as you sleep is uncomfortable if adjusted tightly enough to be sure it stays on. Second, the relative sleep quality it "calculates" differs significantly from my own perception of how well I slept. Even a very bad night (in my view) rated 97%! I no longer bother with it at night. Perhaps I don't understand how to use it most effectively.
Initially I had thought I'd order another for my wife once I tried it out. Now, I'm not sure it's worth the price to have two.

Then I got this headgear, since our gym started a headgear only policy if you wanted to spar.

The headgear, now worn for one full session, really does lessen the blows quite a bit. You feel the hits sure enough.

I am pretty sure unless it's a real hard hit to the button, you're not going to experience a concussive knockout with this nice little piece of kit.

zzlamb Brown Basic Water-Repellent Down Alternative Camping Blanket, Compact Lightweight Polyester Blanket, Portable Quilt Indoor & Outdoor Couch Airplane Car Travel Hiking Backpacking Beach, 45x80in Both sides of this are made of a water-resistant material, as you would find on a sleeping bag or jacket. I would not describe these as being soft or cozy. These are targeted at being travel blankets that should stay cleaner and drier for longer. A negative to this material is that it blocks moisture from escaping, so you can end up sweaty, especially if you are sleeping in a car without any airflow. This stores nicely in a case that can be used as a pillow. I got both the down and down alternative blankets. The down alternative blanket is thinner due to less filler material used. Both are sufficiently warm. The down alternative version should be more resistant to accumulating allergens. The down version offers more padding if you are lying down on this. Neither version offers significant padding if you are lying down on these as the filler is not dense enough to support body weight. The 45 x 80 size is enough to cover one adult unless you are obese. I washed both in a washing machine, and they came out fine.

My sleeping bag is made out of the same material on one side, and has more comfortable cotton on the inner side, with significantly more filling. It can completely unzip to use as a blanket. Depending on the scenario, a sleeping bag can be more versatile, although it takes up more room and is not designed to be used alternatively as a pillow.
text_fidelity_b: zzlamb Brown Basic Water-Repellent Down Alternative Camping Blanket, Compact Lightweight Polyester Blanket, Portable Quilt Indoor & Outdoor Couch Airplane Car Travel Hiking Backpacking Beach, 45x80in

text_fidelity_a:
Desantis Nylon Ambidextrous Pocket Holster, Black I have carried a NAA five shot .22 magnum in my pocket ever since Florida allowed concealed weapons carry. Being small and constructed of stainless steel makes it a perfect hot weather weapon to have with you regardless of how light your clothing is. There are not many firearms that you can carry completely concealed in a swimming suit. Loading it with the new .22 magnum defense rounds gives you five shots that can do a surprising amount of damage to an attacker. I certainly wouldn't want to be hit by it -- and having it beats having nothing.

When it became available, I decided to put the new LaserLyte grip on this gun so that I could extend my effective defensive area. The short barrel makes it pretty ineffective to use rapidly on any target beyond about 7 yards. Adding the LaserLyte allows you to hit point of aim quite a bit further out. The problem I encountered is that while carrying it unholstered in my pocket the laser would bump out of alignment. Not a good thing if you have to depend on it eventually.

So I purchased this Desantis Pocket Holster to protect it. Unfortunately this Desantis holster will not fit around the laser grips. But I also noticed that when the NAA .22 magnum was placed in the holster, the holster was too tight to allow coverage of the trigger. That's not good either. After looking at the holster for a while, I realized that I would have to remove three partial rows of stitching to make it fit. However that would result in the gun sliding around in the holster. After the integrity of the stitching is compromised, it would just be a matter of time before it continued to unwind. Since the holster is designed to stay around the gun as you pull it out of your pocket, it is necessary to make another move to pull the holster from the gun. The Sticky Holster that I use with my Kahr CM9 stays in my pocket when I draw the gun. And the Sticky Holster is about the same size as this Desantis although the Sticky has a much larger space for holding the gun.

Looks like I'll be contacting Sticky Holster instead. I am really happy with their products and I feel very comfortable that they will make a holster to properly fit this combination.

NOTE: 5/11/16 I ordered the proper Sticky Holster after emailing the company and telling them about my problem. They told me to order the holster designed to fit the NAA Pug. It fits perfectly, the trigger is properly covered, and the gun pulls out of the holster leaving the holster in your pocket. Good Job Sticky!
text_fidelity_b: Desantis Nylon Ambidextrous Pocket Holster, Black
